## Verdict

**Dorado** costs least for a team of 9, at **$171 per month**. Its 1-seat minimum means the team pays for exactly 9 seats, which offsets its $19 headline rate — the highest on the list. Inkwell, at $8 per seat, lands close behind at $80 only because its 10-seat minimum adds a single unused seat; in fact Inkwell is cheaper. Correction below.

## Vendors

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $19 | 1 |
| Inkwell | $8 | 10 |
| Borealis | $12 | 25 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 9 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Inkwell:** minimum 10 > 9, so 10 seats paid. 10 × $8 = **$80 per month**. One unused seat, worth $8.
- **Dorado:** minimum 1 < 9, so 9 seats paid. 9 × $19 = **$171 per month**.
- **Borealis:** minimum 25 > 9, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $12 = **$300 per month**. Sixteen unused seats, worth $192.

**Inkwell is cheapest at $80 per month**, $91 below Dorado and $220 below Borealis — $1,092 and $2,640 per year. Effective cost per actual user: Inkwell $8.89 ($80 ÷ 9), Dorado $19.00, Borealis $33.33 ($300 ÷ 9).

## Risks

Inkwell's lead widens with growth: past 10 seats its minimum stops binding and it bills a flat $8 against Dorado's $19. Below 10 people the $80 floor holds, so a team shrinking to 4 or fewer would find Dorado cheaper.

Borealis is not price-competitive at any size in this range; it only reaches its list rate at 25 seats, where it still costs $300 against Inkwell's $200.

This compares list price only. The price list carries no feature, support, or contract detail, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual terms and discounts are not listed and could reorder the result.
